title: Extractive Summarization of Long Documents by Combining Global and Local Context
answer_short: Global context refers to the whole document, while local context refers to the information within the current topic or section.
answer_rationale: The document defines global context as the representation of the entire document (e.g., via a bi-directional GRU encoding the whole text) and local context as the information specific to the topic or section a sentence belongs to (e.g., captured using LSTM-Minus on topic segments). This distinction is explicitly made in the introduction and elaborated in the model architecture section.
